blocks.tk: Köneürgenç Türkmenistanyň demirgazygynda, Daşoguz welaýatynda, Amyderýanyň çep kenaryna ýakyn ýerleşýär. Häzir bu kiçi şäher, ýöne asyrlaryň dowamynda bu ýerde Horezmiň paýtagty bolupdyr. 2005-nji ýylda gadymy şäheriň galyndylary UNESKO-nyň Bütindünýä mirasynyň sanawyna girdi. Sanawa gireli bäri, bu ýere dürli ýurtlardan syýahatçylar gelýärler.
blocks.en: Köneürgenç lies in the north of Turkmenistan, in Dashoguz province, close to the left bank of the Amu Darya. Today it is a small town of some 37,000 people (2022 census), but for centuries this was the capital of Khorezm, the oasis on the river's lower course. In 2005 the ruins of the old city, listed as Kunya-Urgench, were put on UNESCO's World Heritage List: about 350 hectares of monuments, mainly from the 11th to the 16th centuries.

blocks.tk: Bu ýerde adamlar örän irden ýaşapdyrlar: arheologlaryň Kyrkmolla depesinde tapan zatlary miladydan öňki 5-nji asyra degişli. 712-nji ýylda Horezme araplar gelipdir. 10–14-nji asyrlarda bu şäher, Gürgenç ýa-da Ürgenç, söwda ýollarynyň ugrunda uly şähere öwrülipdir. 12-nji asyrda we 13-nji asyryň başynda ol Horezmşalar döwletiniň paýtagty bolupdyr. Mongollar gelmezden öň, Gürgenç Merkezi Aziýanyň iň baý şäherleriniň biri bolupdyr.
blocks.en: People settled here early: the Kyrkmolla mound has a fortress whose finds go back to the 5th century BCE. The Arabs reached Khorezm in 712. Between the 10th and 14th centuries the city, called Gurganj and later Urgench, grew great on the trade routes. In the 12th and early 13th centuries it was the capital of the Khwarazmshahs, whose empire reached as far as Iran, and before the Mongols came, ICOMOS notes, it was the second city of Central Asia after Bukhara.

blocks.tk: 1221-nji ýylda Çingiz hanyň goşuny şäheri weýran edipdir. Ýöne adamlar ony gaýtadan gurupdyrlar we 14-nji asyrda, Altyn Ordanyň döwründe, şäher ýene gülläp ösüpdir. Ibn Battuta 1334-nji ýylda bu ýerden geçipdir we ony türkleriň iň uly, iň owadan şäheri hasaplapdyr. Teýmuryň goşuny 1388-nji ýylda şäheri ýene weýran edipdir. Soňra Amyderýanyň ugry üýtgäpdir. Suw az bolandan soň, adamlar şäherden gidipdirler. 16-njy asyrda Horezmiň paýtagty Hywa göçüpdir. Gadymy şäher üç asyrdan gowrak boş durupdyr, adamlar ony gonamçylyk hökmünde ulanypdyrlar.
blocks.en: In 1221 the armies of Genghis Khan destroyed the city. It was rebuilt and flourished again in the 14th century under the Golden Horde: Ibn Battuta, passing through in 1334, counted it the largest and most beautiful city of the Turks. Timur's troops sacked it in 1379 and razed it in 1388. Then the Amu Darya changed its course; the city lost its water and declined, and in the 16th century the capital of Khorezm moved to Khiva. For more than three centuries the old city stood empty and served as a cemetery, which, UNESCO notes, helped its ruins survive.

blocks.tk: Häzir bu ýeriň iň meşhur ýadygärligi Gutlug Temir minarasy. Onuň beýikligi 60 metr töweregi. Minaranyň aşagy giň, ýokarsy dar, diwarlarynda bolsa kerpiçden owadan nagyşlar bar. Gutlug Temir 14-nji asyrda Altyn Orda üçin Horezmi dolandyrypdyr. Alymlar minaranyň ýaşy barada dürli pikirde: käbirleriniň pikirine görä, ony 11-nji asyryň başynda gurupdyrlar, beýlekileriň pikirine görä, ony 14-nji asyrda gutarypdyrlar.
blocks.en: The best-known monument is the minaret of Kutlug Timur, about 60 m high, 12 m across at the base and 2 m at the top, wrapped in bands of patterned brick. Its date is debated. ICOMOS, UNESCO's advisers, date it to the early 11th century; AramcoWorld describes it as completed in the 14th century, and Wikipedia notes a restoration around 1330. It bears the name of Kutlug Timur, who governed Khorezm for the Golden Horde from 1321 to 1336.

blocks.tk: Minaranyň golaýynda Törebeg hanymyň kümmeti bar. Ol bu ýerdäki kümmetleriň iň ulusy. Rowaýata görä, Törebeg hanym Gutlug Temiriň aýaly bolupdyr. Kümmetiň gümmeziniň içi gök, ak we sary nagyşlardan doly. Bu ýerde Il Arslanyň we Tekeşiň kümmetleri hem bar: olar Horezmşalaryň döwründen, 12-nji asyrdan galypdyr. Nejmeddin Kubranyň kümmetine her ýyl köp zyýaratçy gelýär.
blocks.en: Near the minaret stands the mausoleum of Törebeg Hanym, the largest at the site, whose dome is lined inside with a mosaic of coloured tiles. Tradition links it to Kutlug Timur's wife; ICOMOS dates the building to about 1360–1380, and AramcoWorld suggests it was built later in the century and given her name. The older mausoleums of Il Arslan (around 1150) and Tekesh (around 1195), with their pointed, faceted roofs, belong to the Khwarazmshahs. The mausoleum of the Sufi teacher Najm ad-Din Kubra draws pilgrims from the whole region; ICOMOS found that most visitors to the site are pilgrims.

blocks.tk: UNESKO-nyň bellemegine görä, Ürgenjiň ussalarynyň gurluşyk usuly Eýrana, Owganystana, soňra Hindistana hem täsir edipdir. Gadymy şäher 1985-nji ýyldan bäri döwlet taryhy-medeni goraghanasy.
blocks.en: UNESCO's listing notes that the design and craftsmanship of Urgench's builders spread to Iran and Afghanistan, and later shaped the architecture of the Mughal Empire in 16th-century India. The ruins have been a state historical and cultural park since 1985.

blocks.title: Reading the Turkmen
blocks.text: The old history is told in `-(Y)pdYr`, since nobody alive saw it: *bolupdyr*, *gurupdyrlar*. Look for this unit's converbs too: *Mongollar gelmezden öň* (before the Mongols came), *suw az bolandan soň* (after the water ran short), *sanawa gireli bäri* (since it entered the list).

questions.q: What happened after the Amu Darya changed its course?
options: the city lost its water and people left
questions.explain: *Suw az bolandan soň, adamlar şäherden gidipdirler*: after the water ran short, people left the city.

questions.q: When were the ruins put on UNESCO's World Heritage List?
questions.explain: 1985 is when the state park was created, and 1388 when Timur's troops razed the city.

questions.q: Why do scholars disagree about the minaret of Kutlug Timur?
questions.explain: *Alymlar minaranyň ýaşy barada dürli pikirde*: early 11th century, or finished in the 14th.

sources.title: Kunya-Urgench
sources.note: In Dashoguz velayat, on the left bank of the Amu Daria; capital of Khorezm; monuments mainly 11th–16th centuries, including a 60 m minaret; influence on Iran, Afghanistan and Mughal India; abandoned for more than three centuries and used as a graveyard; state park created in 1985

sources.title: Kunya-Urgench (Turkmenistan), No 1199: ICOMOS evaluation
sources.note: Kyrkmolla, 5th century BCE; the Arabs in 712; 12th-century capital, second city of Central Asia after Bukhara; destroyed in 1221 and rebuilt; Timurid destruction 1372–1388; capital moved to Khiva in the 16th century; about 353 ha; minaret c. 1000–1030, about 60 m; Il-Arslan c. 1150, Tekesh c. 1195, Turabek-Khanum c. 1360–1380; most visitors are pilgrims

sources.title: Konye-Urgench
